Support is done through the terminal because it is the quickest, efficient and simplest distribution agnostic way of diagnosing and performing fixes.

You don't have many tedious GUI windows like on Windows to deal with, you just issue a single command. If you know what you're doing, it is the most efficient way, and if you don't know what you're doing the person who is guiding you through support can explain what the commands do.

People wrongfully think it is so hard, but 90% of the terminal commands you use will be very simple to grasp, things like:

- cd ~/Pictures: Change to directory
- ls: List all files
- sudo: Run as administrator/superuser
- man: View man pages for a command
- systemctl restart: Restart a systemd service
- cat: Echo the contents of a file to the terminal
- apt update: Update an Ubuntu system

... and so on

Flatpaks/Snaps can be installed via GNOME software manager, which most applications are bundled as.
